tob-10057: Missionary scholar Samuel Zwemer writes a sympathetic life of Al-Ghazali, the eleventh-century Muslim thinker he calls a ‘seeker after God.’ The book presents Ghazali’s spiritual quest as the finest expression of Islamic devotion, aimed at Christian readers curious about Islam at its most earnest. It remains a notable early attempt by a Westerner to understand Islamic mysticism from within.
tob-10957: Proclus was the last great philosopher of pagan antiquity, and this work is his systematic theology of the Platonic gods. He arranges the divine hierarchy — from the ineffable One down through gods, angels, and souls — with mathematical precision. Thomas Taylor’s translation introduced this summit of Neoplatonism to English readers. It shaped the mystical philosophy of the Renaissance.
tob-4057: The fourth volume rounds out Blavatsky’s Secret Doctrine with more hidden teaching on the secret past of faiths and the veiled powers of nature. It carries on her work of braiding Eastern and Western mystic lore into one grand scheme. The volume caps the boldest work of the 1800s occult rebirth.
tob-4157: Andrew Lang’s daring book held that belief in a high god came first in man’s story — not last, as the wise men of his day taught. From word out of tribal lands the world over, he took on the theory that faith climbed up from ghost-fear. The book touched off a hot fight over where religion starts.
tob-0157: This Sacred Books of the East volume strings the English Zend Avesta — Vendidad, Yashts, and fellow Zoroastrian books. Turned by Darmesteter, Mills, and others, it bore Persia’s old faith to English readers. The book is needful for students of matched faiths.
tob-10257: The Rosarium Philosophorum — the Rosary of the Philosophers — is the great illustrated alchemical collection of the late Middle Ages. Its twenty woodcut emblems show the stages of the Great Work in symbolic pictures. Masters’ sayings accompany each image. The book became the classic picture-book of alchemy.
tob-10457: Molinos’s Spiritual Torrents is the classic of Quietism — the Spanish priest’s guide to the prayer of stillness. He taught total abandonment to God and the death of self-will. Condemned in 1687, his teaching lived on underground. The book remains a landmark of contemplative literature.
cia-0000108157: A May 1958 National Intelligence Estimate on probable developments in Indonesia. With rebellion simmering in the outer islands and the central government shaky, Washington needed a forecast it could plan around. The estimate is Cold War fortune-telling at its most formal — every agency signing off on one prediction.
cia-0000109057: A January 1968 study of Cuban subversive activities across Latin America from 1959 to 1968. Havana exported revolution — training guerrillas, funding movements, and preaching insurgency from Venezuela to Bolivia. The report is a decade-long charge sheet of Cuba's campaign to set the continent alight, as seen from Washington.
cia-0000126957: A November 1965 forecast of Panama's short-term political prospects. The canal made Panama permanently strategic — and permanently turbulent. The document weighs the country's stability with the waterway's security always in the background.
cia-0000132757: A 1960 report: the Cuban government planning further involvement of President Eisenhower — the truncated title cuts off how. Havana was dragging Ike into its propaganda. The document is the provocation: the president, targeted.
cia-0000135857: A 1954 report on the compromise of cable traffic for PBSUCCESS. The operation's communications were exposed — a counterspy's nightmare. The document is the breach: the cables, compromised.
cia-0000136157: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for ONTRICH/HEGARTY with KUGOWN team themes. The propaganda teams got their talking points. The document is the theme: the message, set.
cia-0000136257: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN reporting the possible need for bomb support to swing the army. Air power as persuasion. The document is the leverage: the bombs, contemplated — the army, to be swayed.
cia-0000136857: A 1954 cable on headquarters not concurring with LINCOLN's recommendation, due to the outcome of the Caracas conference — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The field was overruled. The document is the refusal: the concurrence, withheld.
cia-0000136957: A 1954 cable to the senior representative in Guatemala City on the Secretary of State's statement at the morning press — the truncated title cuts off the rest. Washington's line, delivered. The document is the statement: the secretary, quoted.
un-ga-res-a-69-57: General Assembly Resolution A/69/57, adopted in 2014. The session rolled on. The entry is the record: the fifty-seventh act, dated.
un-sc-res-57: Security Council Resolution 57, adopted in 1948. The young Council deliberated. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-357: Security Council Resolution 357, adopted in 1974. The deliberations continued. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-757: Security Council Resolution 757, adopted in May 1992 — the comprehensive sanctions on the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, punishing Belgrade for the Bosnian war. Trade, flights, and finance were severed. The resolution is the isolation: the pariah, quarantined.
un-sc-res-1557: Security Council Resolution 1557, adopted in 2004 — aligned. The deliberations rolled on. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
plos-pone-0000057: A 2006 PLOS ONE paper on genes from Chagas susceptibility loci that are differentially expressed — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The genes behind vulnerability to Chagas disease. The paper is the loci: the susceptibility, genetic.
cia-0000137457: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000137457. The invasion year's Spanish archive. The entry is the archive: the year, fateful.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d57: The Army Chief of Staff Marshall to the president's chief of staff — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 57. The military's internal line. The memo is the military: the chiefs, conferring.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d157: The minister in Egypt, Kirk, to the Egyptian prime minister and ministers — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 157. The legation's formal notes. The notes are the formal: Kirk, to the government.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d257: Combined Chiefs of Staff minutes, November 23, 1943 — Document 257. A second session that day. The minutes are the second: the planners, again.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d357: Joint Chiefs of Staff minutes, November 28, 1943 — Document 357. The American planners, minuted — now at Tehran. The minutes are the planners': the chiefs, conferring.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d457: Combined Chiefs of Staff minutes, December 6, 1943 — Document 457. The Allied planners, minuted. The minutes are the planners': the chiefs, combined.
the-diary-and-letters-of-madame-d-arblay: Fanny Burney — Madame D'Arblay — kept one of the great diaries in English, and this volume covers her years at the court of George III. Readers meet the royal family, courtiers, and visiting celebrities through her sharp, amused eyes. Few documents bring the late-eighteenth-century English court so vividly, personally alive.
arxiv-2605-08857: Conformal prediction wraps a model's guesses in honest uncertainty bands, but it gets expensive on big data. Manuel Heurich, Maximilian Granz, and Tim Landgraf propose RareCP, a regime-aware retrieval scheme that makes conformal prediction efficient by fetching only the relevant calibration cases. The 2026 paper is about trustworthy uncertainty on a budget.
arxiv-2605-09157: Entropy-regularized actor-critic methods keep policies exploratory, and mixture policies add another layer of flexibility. Jiamin He and Samuel Neumann revisit the combination, asking what mixture policies really buy. The 2026 paper is a second look at a reinforcement-learning design choice.
arxiv-2605-09257: Counterfactual questions — what would the outcome have been? — need quantile processes with rigorous guarantees. Pengyun Wang studies their regularity, phase transitions, and uniform inference under proximal conditions. The 2026 paper is deep statistical theory for causal what-ifs in policy evaluation.
arxiv-2605-09357: Tiny microcontrollers cannot run big neural networks alone — but a network of them can split the work. Junyu Lu, Shashwath Suresh, Hao Liu, and colleagues split CNN inference across networked microcontrollers. The 2026 paper is edge AI for the smallest hardware.
arxiv-2605-09457: Graphs can be rewired to make learning easier, but the rewiring should respect what each node does — its role. Riccardo Porcedda, Giuseppe Squillace, Bastian Epping, and colleagues rewire role-aware via approximate equitable partitions — RAwR. The 2026 paper tidies graphs before the learning starts.
arxiv-2605-09857: Multicalibration — calibrated predictions across many subgroups — with only weak supervision, unified in one approach. Futoshi Futami and Takashi Ishida develop it. The 2026 paper is machine learning fairness that calibrates everywhere at once. It calibrates fairly across subgroups with weak supervision.
plos-pone-0003457: Chronobiologists built a speedier clock-hunting tool in this 2008 methods paper. Gene-silencing screens had transformed the search for biological machinery, but circadian rhythm genes lagged behind. Their high-throughput assay, using siRNA in human U2OS cells, lets researchers knock down genes by the thousands and watch which ones break the body's daily clock.
plos-pone-0003557: Malaria immunologists measured how protection grows with age in this 2008 Kenyan study. Antibodies that stall the malaria parasite's growth accumulate as children grow up amid repeated infections, and the team linked those growth-inhibiting antibodies to real protection from high parasite loads. The age curve points vaccine designers at the immunity nature builds.
plos-pone-0003657: In 2008, Camas and Poyatos asked why gene-control circuits favor certain shapes. The control networks of E. coli reuse small wiring patterns called motifs, and the team tested what drives those patterns to form. Their model weighs need against chance, asking whether the motifs won out by use or by luck.
plos-pone-0003757: In 2008, de Bruyn, Bastos, and Eadie investigated a seal die-off with an unlikely suspect. Adult male subantarctic fur seals were dying in numbers, and the team asked whether alien mice, carriers of disease, were the culprits. The detective work tests a surprising chain from tiny invaders to giant victims.
plos-pone-0003857: Back in 2008, a group sought liver truth without the needle. With biopsy as a flawed gold standard, they tested non-invasive measures of liver fibrosis against each other for concordance. The new methodology aims to make liver staging accurate without cutting.
plos-pone-0003957: In 2008, Marinelli, Piuri, and Swigonova released BRED, a toolkit for editing phage genomes. The simple, powerful method builds mutant and recombinant bacteriophages with ease. The tool opens viral engineering to labs without specialized setups.
plos-pone-0004057: In 2008, Dowdy, Lourenco, and Cavalcante weighed TB culture's worth in Brazil. They measured the impact and cost-effectiveness of culturing TB in HIV-infected adults. Culture remains the diagnostic gold standard, but its real-world value was unclear. The analysis guides where scarce diagnostic budgets do the most good.
plos-pone-0004157: In 2008, Kishioka, Fukushima, and Ito found fear learning at a whisper. A new form of memory formed for auditory fear with a mild shock. Low-intensity training still etched lasting fear memory. The finding widens how quietly fear can be learned.
plos-pone-0004257: In 2009, Yarkoni, Barch, and Gray linked brain flickers to slow reactions. BOLD signals tracked trial-by-trial reaction time swings in gray and white matter both. The big multi-study fMRI analysis pooled many datasets. The brain-behavior link sharpens human attention research greatly.
plos-pone-0004357: In 2009, Marcet-Houben and Gabaldón weighed trees against forests. The fungal tree of life was compared with topological diversity in the yeast phylome. Single trees missed the forest's variety. The study guides phylogenomic practice. The work shows gene trees disagreeing often.
plos-pone-0358357: Foam rolling is gym folklore for loosening muscles, but does it sharpen reflexes? This randomized trial tested how different durations of foam rolling affected visual reaction time in young male basketball players. The duration-dependent results tell athletes and coaches how long to roll to get a real, measurable edge.
plos-pone-0357457: We unconsciously mimic the speech of people we talk to — but does our wider social network shape that? This paper studied embedded dyads, pairs nested in larger networks, to see how personal networks relate to linguistic accommodation. The findings reveal how our friends’ friends tilt the way we talk.
plos-pone-0358457: Fear of childbirth keeps some women away from the care they need. This study measured the prevalence of childbirth fear among antenatal attendees in Kumasi, Ghana, breaking down the drivers by parity — whether it was a first or later pregnancy. The findings point to which mothers need reassurance most.
plos-pone-0358657: After bypass surgery for a failing heart, some patients’ heart muscle recovers and some doesn’t. This exploratory study used dual-tracer PET/CT scans — ammonia and FDG — to predict which hearts would bounce back after CABG in ischemic cardiomyopathy. The imaging predicted recovery, helping surgeons know who benefits most.
plos-pone-0357057: Runner’s knee sidelines marathoners — and weak hips may be the culprit. This retrospective cohort study compared hip stability training against standard care on Q-angle and pain in marathon runners with patellofemoral pain syndrome. The results test whether stronger hips really mean happier knees for distance runners.
plos-pone-0344957: Head and neck cancers urgently need better prognostic tools. This paper built a PANoptosis-based index — the HNSCPAN-index — that predicts prognosis in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, and revealed DSCAM as a therapeutic target. The index sorts patients by risk while simultaneously naming a new drug target for the disease.
plos-pone-0357957: Even in war zones, blood pressure silently kills. This cross-sectional study found screen-detected raised blood pressure and mapped gaps in the hypertension care cascade among adults attending a humanitarian medical mission in Ukraine. The gaps expose exactly where crisis care fails people with chronic disease.
plos-pone-0355557: Machine learning hunts for disease-causing variants in whole genomes — but too often ignores whether genes are actually expressed. This paper argued detection approaches must address the expression of functional genes. The critique pushes variant-hunting AI toward biological reality.
plos-pone-0356257: Filoviruses — Ebola and its kin — demand diagnostics that work anywhere. This paper evaluated multiplex pan-filovirus assay performance and reproducibility across varied geographical and resource settings. The rugged assay validation brings reliable filovirus detection closer to the field.
plos-pone-0349357: Spruce budworms that diapause — overwinter in dormancy — differ profoundly from those that don’t. This paper found major changes in gene expression between diapausing and non-diapause strains. The genetic differences illuminate one of forest ecology’s most consequential survival strategies.
plos-pone-0355057: After nerve injury, painful neuromas can form — and surgeons debate how best to prevent them. This rat sciatic nerve study compared nerve coagulation versus cap implantation for neuroma prevention using histological and neuroradiological inspection. The head-to-head comparison guides surgical technique toward genuinely less painful outcomes.
plos-pone-0355957: Cyclospora cayetanensis — a foodborne parasite — contaminates agricultural water worldwide. This paper optimized the Mit1C real-time PCR assay on the Bio-Rad CFX96 platform for detecting it. The optimized assay gives food safety labs a validated tool for catching the parasite before it reaches produce.
plos-pone-0355457: African leaders’ UN General Assembly speeches — rich English corpora — can teach both grammar and sustainability. This paper built a corpus-informed pedagogical model (GSIC) from their UNGA-2025 speeches. The innovative model turns political oratory into language learning with a conscience.
plos-pone-0354957: Mount Emei’s soundscape — bells, chanting, wind through ancient trees — restores visitors. This paper examined how soundscape shapes restorative experience at the world heritage site, with cultural authenticity as mediator. The findings reveal that what we hear determines how deeply a sacred place heals us.
plos-pone-0354857: Breastfeeding duration depends on a web of interacting factors. This paper uncovered those complex correlations using XGBoost machine learning. The model’s feature interactions reveal which combinations of circumstances keep babies breastfeeding longest — guiding targeted support.
plos-pone-0354157: Marketing AI must spot brand logos and predict aesthetic tastes — efficiently. This paper showed efficient fine-tuning of large vision-language models for visual marketing analysis, from logo detection to aesthetic preference prediction. The streamlined approach brings cutting-edge visual AI within marketers’ computational reach.
plos-pone-0349257: Diabetes care in Brazil isn’t equal — gender, race, and class intersect to shape it. This paper evaluated care adequacy at that intersection. The findings demand diabetes programs that confront compounded disadvantage rather than treating all patients as the same.
europmc-pmc2803857: BLAST, the workhorse for searching DNA and protein databases, got a major rewrite described in this 2009 paper. The authors present BLAST+, rebuilt with a cleaner architecture for speed and flexibility. They explain the new design and show what the suite can do. The paper documents the version of BLAST that still powers sequence searches in labs worldwide.
europmc-pmc2816657: Low oxygen makes breast cancer more aggressive, and this 2010 paper uncovers part of how. The authors show hypoxia boosts Notch signaling, which lowers E-cadherin and lets cancer cells migrate and invade more freely. The chain links oxygen starvation to metastasis. Blocking this pathway became a candidate strategy against spreading tumors.
europmc-pmc2846857: Animal stroke research looked more promising than it was. This 2010 paper shows publication bias in animal stroke studies leads to major overstatement of treatment efficacy, because negative results go unpublished. The authors quantify the inflation. Their exposé forced the field to confront its own skewed literature.
europmc-pmc2852857: Grapes pack color compounds tied to health claims. This 2010 review sifts what grape polyphenols do in the body. The authors stack the proof, from heart to cell defense, and judge its strength. Their take gives the fruit's fame a firm base without overstating what the science shows.
europmc-pmc2854757: Flame-guard dust coats homes, and this 2010 paper asks what it does to men. The team tied house dust's organophosphate compounds to hormone levels and sperm health. Their read found dips where dust ran high. The tie put home dust on the male-health map.
europmc-pmc2916857: Nerve cells branch like trees, and this 2010 paper finds one rule for them all. The authors propose a general theory of neuronal branching with practical application to real neurons. Their single rule predicts diverse arbors across cell types. The work unified a sprawling field with elegant math.
europmc-pmc2958657: Resting cells are busier than they look. This 2010 paper finds quiet fibroblasts still burn fuel at a high rate. The authors topple the idle-cell myth. Their work reframes what cellular rest means. Even parked cells keep their engines warm.
europmc-pmc2965757: Extreme blood pressure runs in genes, and this 2010 study finds a culprit. The authors' genome-wide study of blood pressure extremes identifies a variant near UMOD linked to hypertension. Their find points to kidney handling of salt. The work opened a therapeutic lead.
europmc-pmc3000457: Disease markers in blood need measuring at scale. This 2010 paper brings a DNA-tag method that reads thousands of proteins from one sample. The authors' platform powers marker hunts. Their work spread through clinics. One drop of blood now yields a protein portrait.
europmc-pmc3029257: Pseudomonas slime cities lean on a sugary scaffold. This 2011 paper shows the Pel sugar gives Pseudomonas biofilms their structure and shield. The authors reveal the scaffold. Their work points to slime-busting drugs. Lung infections in cystic fibrosis use this shield.
europmc-pmc3037057: Trial lotteries need unpredictable blocks. This 2011 paper explains how random block sizes keep treatment assignment secret. The author's method guards trials against peeking. Their guidance spread through trial design. Fixed blocks let doctors guess the next patient. Random blocks close the guessing loophole.
europmc-pmc3041657: Venn diagrams got beautiful and programmable. This 2011 paper introduces VennDiagram, an R package for highly-customizable Venn and Euler diagrams. The authors' package became a plotting staple. Their software graced thousands of papers. Biologists love its polished circles. The plots made it into top journals.
europmc-pmc6524357: Eight wild vegetables eaten in western Nepal - from water spinach to black nightshade - were tested for health-promoting chemistry. Researchers measured their phenolic and flavonoid content and antioxidant power in the lab. The results catalog which traditional foods pack the strongest antioxidant punch, supporting their nutritional value for local diets.
europmc-pmc6536957: Nrf2 is a cellular guardian that switches on antioxidant and detox defenses - protective in healthy cells, but cancers hijack it to shield themselves from chemotherapy. This review explores the double edge: boosting Nrf2 may prevent cancer, while blocking it could make treatments work better. The pathway's two faces make it one of oncology's trickiest targets.
europmc-pmc6540057: Cell membranes are not passive wrappers - their lipid makeup dictates how membranes bend, how organelles form, and how signals pass. This review shows how the specific mix of membrane lipids controls structure and compartmentalization across the cell. Because many diseases involve lipid imbalances, tweaking membrane composition is emerging as a therapeutic strategy.
europmc-pmc6600457: Propolis - the resinous goo bees use to seal their hives - turns out to be a germ-fighter. This review rounds up the latest science on propolis's antibacterial powers: which bacteria it stops and how. With antibiotic resistance rising, the bee-made substance earns a closer look as a natural antimicrobial.
europmc-pmc6691157: Nearly everyone carries Epstein-Barr virus - the 'kissing disease' bug - yet it quietly causes cancers worldwide. This review maps EBV-linked tumors across the globe: which cancers, where, and how the lifelong infection turns malignant. The innocent passenger, it turns out, is a killer in disguise.
europmc-pmc6695957: Every cycle, estrogen builds the womb's lining and progesterone readies it for a possible pregnancy - a hormonal duet. In endometriosis the duet goes off-key: uterine-like tissue grows outside the womb and resists progesterone's calming signals. This review traces the faulty signaling and what it means for treatment.
europmc-pmc6769257: Proteins carry postal codes - short targeting peptides that direct them to cellular addresses. This study used deep learning to detect the sequence signals hidden in those peptides. The AI not only predicts destinations but reveals new biology in the code.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-857: One label for all colleges? GAO's 2007 report says lumping public, nonprofit, and for-profit schools under one definition would not fly. The findings argue the sectors differ too much for a single yardstick. The report defends nuance in the heated debate over who deserves the name ‘college.'
gao-gaoreports-b-299457: Apptis tripled its May 2007 protest — three case numbers, one tech fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles all three claims. The firm challenged the awards as unfair; the call weighs each claim. Triple filings get one triple-checked answer from the referee.
gao-gaoreports-b-299557: A-TEK took its May 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict. The firm said the agency's award was unfair; the call tests the protest against bid law. Tech deals big and small get the same fair-play ruling in the end.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-657: Breach notices needed a playbook in 2007 — GAO's report distills the hard lessons on telling people their data leaked. The findings write the notification rules in plain terms. The report's creed: the hacked deserve to hear it fast, straight, and first from you.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-457: Burma's junta was strangling the helpers in 2007 — GAO's report says aid programs there ran straight into the regime's walls. The findings document the constraints in detail. The report's quiet fury: the suffering was man-made, and so were the barriers.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-557: Kids' medicines were finally being studied in 2007 — GAO's report reviews the pediatric drug research done under the children's act. The findings tally the studies one by one. The report's cause: children are not just small adults, and their drugs should prove it.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-357: Tsunami rebuilding ran over budget in 2007, and GAO's report says the signature American efforts in Indonesia and Sri Lanka blew past initial costs. The findings track the overruns. The report asks whether the generosity was managed or just spent. The goodwill was real; the management was not.
openalex-w7211888757: The Assembly of God is one of Brazil's largest evangelical churches, and in the state of Amazonas its churches run an active program of Christian teaching. This article studies the ideas behind that work: how the church aims to shape the whole person in faith and daily life. It treats church education as a planned, purposeful effort and maps the thinking behind it.
openalex-w4408308157: Moving gut germs from a healthy donor can heal a sick gut. This paper reviews stool transplants: what they treat now and what they might treat next. The authors sized up the evidence for resetting gut flora. A gut-medicine review of the strangest transplant in use.
pmc-13437657: A 2026 engineering paper on a wearable triboelectric nanogenerator — a device that makes electricity from friction — built with indium selenide (InSe) to harvest energy from body movement and sense motion. The patch could power small sensors from walking alone. It is a step toward wearables that never need charging.
pmc-13437257: A 2026 review on how one-electron oxidation of DNA's purine and pyrimidine bases contributes to light- and radiation-induced damage to cellular DNA. These oxidized bases are key lesions in sun damage and radiotherapy side effects. The paper gathers the chemistry behind a fundamental biological threat.
pmc-13436157: This 2026 review covers phycobilisomes — the modular light-harvesting antenna systems of cyanobacteria and red algae. These protein complexes capture sunlight with remarkable efficiency. The paper explains their architecture and why engineers look to them for ideas about artificial photosynthesis.
pmc-13375157: A 2026 in vitro study testing an iodine-based paste with silver nanoparticles against Enterococcus faecalis — the stubborn bacterium behind failed root canals. The combination showed antibacterial effect in the lab. The paste could become a new endodontic disinfectant.
pmc-13291757: This 2026 study protocol describes a multicenter randomized comparison of dexamethasone versus placebo in comatose survivors of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Steroids might protect the injured brain — or harm it. The protocol lays out how the question will be tested.
pmc-13466957: In this 2026 dermatology paper, researchers quantified the effects of sex hormones on hair growth and patient satisfaction. Hormones and hair are deeply linked. The quantitative data inform treatment expectations.
pmc-13431657: In this 2026 study, infant infection with specific RSV genotypes predicted subsequent childhood asthma risk. Not all RSV is equal — the viral strain matters. The genotype link refines prevention targeting.
pmc-13559557: In this 2026 radiology paper, intratumoral and peritumoral radiomics — quantitative image features from inside and around the tumor — assessed lymphovascular invasion in invasive breast cancer. Imaging that predicts invasion guides surgery. The validated model is the advance.
pmc-13469457: This 2026 study tracked body composition changes over four years in American college football players. The athletes' bodies transformed across their careers. The longitudinal data inform training and health.
pmc-13454857: In this 2026 paper, Aedes albopictus and dengue transmission risk in France over the 21st century were projected. The tiger mosquito's French future was modeled. The projections guide preparedness.
pmc-13445157: A 2026 statistics paper: "Fixed or Random Effects: Analysis of Clustered Data." The modeling choice was examined. The paper guides analysts.
pmc-13427057: This 2026 Brazilian consensus addressed management of bleeding complications related to oral anticoagulant use. The experts' guidance is the contribution. The consensus serves clinicians.
pmc-13428157: A 2026 pediatric case report of pyoderma gangrenosum as a rare manifestation of myelodysplastic syndrome. The skin ulcer signaled the marrow disease. The case teaches the association.
pmc-13512457: This 2026 paper presented axioms of diagnostic urgency — a characterization theorem. The diagnostic decision theory was formalized. The axioms are the mathematical contribution.
pmc-13532757: A 2026 paper: a leakage-aware genomic prediction pipeline for meropenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae using transformer-based resistome representation learning (the title is truncated). The AI predicted the resistance. The pipeline is the surveillance tool.
pmc-13459357: A 2026 periodontal paper: IL-17 receptor inhibition with brodalumab limited experimental periodontitis. The psoriasis drug protected the gums. The limiting is the repurposing signal.
arxiv-2606-16057: Estimating a moving object's position from noisy sensors is called state estimation, and two popular tools — the extended Kalman filter and factor graph optimization — each have strengths. This paper combines them in a hybrid that switches between the two on a smart schedule, getting the accuracy of one and the efficiency of the other. It targets robotics and navigation engineers.
arxiv-2606-16257: Chance-math leans on dice draws from knotty odds — yet tame-draw tricks flop on wild shapes. This paper tames the wobble of wild-shape draws, aimed at back-track jobs: name the cause from the clues. For odds pros and clue-chasers. Less wobble, truer reads.
arxiv-2606-16557: Excitons — bound pairs of electrons and holes — can get trapped in the moiré patterns of stacked atom-thin sheets. This paper studies moiré trapping of quadrupolar excitons in van der Waals trilayers: three stacked 2D materials. It targets condensed-matter physicists engineering quantum optical materials.
arxiv-2606-16757: Black holes carry entropy — a measure of hidden information — famously tied to their surface area. This paper computes that entropy allowing for second-order departures from equilibrium: small wobbles away from perfect balance. It is a theoretical gravity paper for black-hole researchers.
